key_insight: PoseBench provides a standardized benchmark showing that modern deep‑learning docking and structure‑prediction models can reach competitive accuracy on many targets but display systematic failure modes and limited generalization compared with physics‑aware approaches.
problem_solved: Fills the gap of a rigorous, standardized benchmark to quantify strengths, limitations, and failure modes of AI‑based protein–ligand docking and structure‑prediction methods.
method: Curated PoseBench: a diverse, well‑annotated dataset of protein–ligand complexes and standardized evaluation protocols.
Benchmarked state‑of‑the‑art deep‑learning docking and structure‑prediction models using metrics like pose RMSD and success rate across target classes.
Performed diagnostic analyses to identify systematic errors and factors that drive performance variation (e.g., ligand size, binding‑site flexibility, model confidence).
impact: Gives AI/ML researchers a reproducible testbed and diagnostic lens to prioritize model improvements, improve generalization, and make safer tool choices for structure‑based drug discovery. It steers development from black‑box gains toward robustness and interpretable failure analysis.
